chunks: Al-Fadl said, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-'Adani, the companion of Sufyan, narrated: He told me, Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi, the companion of Abu Yusuf, from Abu Yusuf: He told me, Layth ibn Abi Sulayman, from Abu 'Amr al-'Abdi, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him):

He used to say: 'The fixed shares (faraid) are from six shares: Two-thirds are four shares, and one-half is three shares, and one-third is two shares, and one-fourth is one and a half shares, and one-eighth is three-quarters of a share. And with the child (descendants), only the parents, the husband, and the wife inherit. And the mother is not barred from the third except by the child and the siblings. And the husband is not increased beyond one-half, nor is the one-fourth decreased. And the wife is not increased beyond one-fourth, nor is the one-eighth decreased. And if there are four or fewer, they are equal in it. And the siblings from the mother are not increased beyond one-third, nor are they decreased from one-sixth, and they are equal in it, male and female. And they are not barred from the third except by the child and the father. And the diya (blood money) is divided among whoever secures the inheritance.'"

Al-Fadl said: And this is a sound hadith in agreement with the Book, and in it is evidence that the brothers and sisters inherit nothing with the child, and the grandfather inherits nothing with the child, and in it is evidence that the mother bars the siblings from the inheritance.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific fractional shares for heirs in Shia inheritance law according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), transmitted through a chain validated by Al-Fadl, articulates the foundational arithmetic of Islamic inheritance (al-Fara'id) based on the 'base of six' (al-Asnam al-Sitta). It serves as a critical juristic proof for Shia and Sunni schools regarding the exclusion of maternal siblings by the mother's share and the specific limitations on spouses and parents, reinforcing the structural integrity of the Quranic distribution system.
